To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a small chimered promoter for prostate‐specific transduction of adenoviral vectors that is active in all prostate cancer cells tested.
we developed a novel chimeric promoter, which is highly active and prostate‐specific.
a small chimered promoter for high and prostatic‐specific expression from adenovirals vectors is constructed and tested.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new gene therapy approach to treat patients suffering from prostate cancer.
the development and evaluation of new methods and techniques in the field of gene and cell therapy for prostate cancer.
the design of a small chimerical promoter for high and tissue‐specific transgene regulation in the human prostate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a small chimered promoter is an efficient tool for high and prostate specific transgene expression from an adenoviral vector.
the small chimeric prostate‐specific promoter (sPSP) has been constructed, characterized and applied in a prostate‐specific adenoviral vector (Ad‐sPSP‐Luc) for high and specific transgene expression.
the use of a small chimeral promoter for adenoviral vectors is a good choice to target the transgene expression in prostate cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chimeric promoter we constructed was highly specific for prostate cancer cells.
we have developed a new promoter that can be used for prostate‐specific transfection.
we constructed a small chimpromoter with high activity in prostate tissue and high specificity for this tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chimeric promoter is highly active and prostate‐specific in vitro and in vivo in the mouse model of the TRAMP mouse.
a small chimered promoter with 5′‐flanking regions of the PSA and the probasin promoters can be used to achieve high and prostate‐ specific gene expression.

we have shown that the combination of the androgen receptor (AR) binding site and the prostate specific element (PSE) from the prostate specific antigen (PSA) gene is a powerful tool for the transcriptional targeting of prostate cancer cells.
